watchOut: The hourly ranges are among the lowest of the base-rate tables we read, so expect a quote above them.
Its page says "instant pricing for any route in the world"; we did not test the tool.
feesNamed: Daily minimum flight time, typically 2 hours
name: evoJets
roleBasis: Its pages talk about "your jet broker" and explain "What Is A Private Jet Broker?" as a description of its own service. We did not find a plain "we do not own aircraft" line on the pages we read.
summary: Charter provider that prints a full itemized sample trip and a six-row hourly table.
differentiator: Shows its arithmetic. A Los Angeles to Aspen round trip in a midsize jet at $3,400 an hour for 5 hours becomes $20,317.50 once a $550 fuel surcharge, $600 crew fees, $750 landing fees and $1,417.50 in excise tax are added.
priceNote: Hourly table labeled "ballpark" and one itemized trip. It also explains that most aircraft carry a 2-hour daily minimum, so a 1-hour flight can bill as 2 hours.
operatorDisclosure: Not stated on the pages we read.
bestFor: Buyers who want to learn how an hourly rate turns into a total before they compare quotes.
skipIf: You need the per-passenger segment fee shown. Its sample trip lists the excise tax but no segment fee line.
